title: The Chicago Defender and the Black press
summary: The Defender was the paper of Black show business, where mail was sent; he mentions the Interstate Tattler gossip sheet.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Uh-huh. How important was say, the Chicago Defender to -- to you when -- back in the '20's, and '30's, was that something you looked forward every week to read?
Oh, yes.
Defender and --
Oh, absolutely, yes.
-- to find out what was happening in the business,
That's right. Yes. We thought that was a great paper.
Because the black show business world
was quite separate from the white.
Oh, absolutely, yes. Yes. Chicago Defender really gave you all the news of the entertainment in Chicago at that time.
Right, and the white papers weren't bothering with that.
-- bothered at all, didn't mean a thing.
And you also, people used to get their mail --
Oh, surely.
-- right through -- at the Chicago Defender?
Absolutely, yes.
But did you read, for instance, white papers?
Well, no, I didn't really didn't. I only read the Chicago Defender.
Uh-huh. And I guess the Amsterdam Newsly Run.
Amsterdam News, the Afro-American.
Do you remember the Interstate Tattler?
Oh, yes.
That was a little gossip sheet, wasn't it?
Gossip sheet, yes. Yes.
And there was a man, let's see what was his name, who -- who ran that paper?
No, no, I don't remember. Right now.
I heard that he was very famous because if you saw him, you sort of made sure you were behaving when he was around, because --
Yes.
-- otherwise it would get in --
I should know who that was, I just tell you -- right now I can't -- you took me back that time, yes. I remember very well, Tattler.
